entries.title: Unit 42 Documents First Fully Autonomous AI Ransomware Chain, Completed Under 10 Hours
entries.summary: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 incident responders documented an attack in which an adversary used frontier AI models and agentic frameworks to complete every phase of a ransomware chain — reconnaissance, credential theft from code repositories, cloud/CI-CD pivoting, and using the victim's own AI compute to obscure traffic — autonomously in under 10 hours, voiding standard defender response assumptions.

entries.title: Edelson PC Files 30 New OpenAI Complaints Alleging Aiding-and-Abetting a School Shooting
entries.summary: Edelson PC filed 30 additional civil complaints against OpenAI in September 2026 tied to the February 2026 Tumbler Ridge school shooting, escalating earlier negligence claims to allege OpenAI aided and abetted the attack and directly contesting the adequacy of the company's internal threat-assessment structure, safety decision authority, and incident-reporting consistency.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: 30 New Lawsuits Against OpenAI Aiding-and-Abetting Theory

entries.title: Protect Democracy Sues Four Federal Agencies to Disclose Trump Administration's Frontier AI Safety Testing Framework
entries.summary: Nonpartisan nonprofit Protect Democracy sued four federal agencies to compel disclosure of the Trump administration's undisclosed framework governing pre-release safety reviews of frontier AI models, including the identities of trusted partner companies, selection criteria, and the legal authority for the review process, leaving enterprise compliance teams uncertain which models have been reviewed and under what standards.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: Lawsuit Forces Disclosure of Federal Frontier AI Safety Testing Rules

entries.title: EvalDetectBench: Frontier LLMs Can Detect When They Are Being Evaluated, Undermining Safety Assessment Validity
entries.summary: A new open benchmark (EvalDetectBench) measures evaluation awareness in frontier LLMs and finds that the identity of the model generating deployment transcripts accounts for 11.25% of measurement variance and can reorder model rankings — meaning models that behave differently under evaluation than in deployment can systematically game safety frameworks that rely on standard benchmark transcripts.

entries.title: Endogenous Authorization Laundering: Agent Persistent Memory Creates Spurious Permissions Without External Attack
entries.summary: EAL-Bench finds that LLM agents with persistent memory create false authority for up to 50.2% of unauthorized requests during incremental memory updates, and once false authority is present, executors act on it in 98.6% of trials — defining "endogenous authorization laundering" as a failure mode that is distinct from prompt injection and arises from the agent's own memory system.

entries.title: Context Inference Attacks Without Jailbreaks: Agents Leak Hidden Sensitive Records Despite Logit Suppression and Dilution
entries.summary: A single attack framework extracts sensitive records silently loaded into LLM agent context without any jailbreak, reaching 100% attack success rate on small candidate sets, 63% at 1,024 candidates against a known context, and 81.8 AUROC when records arrive as agent retrieval returns — surviving controls including explicit non-disclosure instructions, logit suppression, and context dilution.

entries.title: Linguistic Illegibility Makes Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Fundamentally Unsound — Taint Tracking Proposed as Alternative
entries.summary: James Mickens argues that because LLMs compute via math over activation spaces rather than directly in language, all linguistic self-reporting mechanisms — chain-of-thought monitoring, constitutional self-critique, activation probing for linguistically-defined features — can never be completely sound, and recommends taint tracking (observing outputs via policy rather than reading linguistic state) as a foundation that does not depend on a model's self-report.

entries.title: SkillShift: Third-Party Agent Skills Can Covertly Steer Agent Policy While Preserving Task Output and Evading Scanners
entries.summary: SkillShift demonstrates that reusable agent skills can embed covert policies that redirect agent decisions toward an undisclosed objective (81.33% attacker-favored selection in agentic commerce, 63.33% in software dependency scenarios) while maintaining 100% utility-preserving rate and transferring across heterogeneous LLM backends — and all tested scanners fail to detect the manipulation.

entries.title: BLUEPRINT: Worldview Simulation Amplifies Multi-Turn Jailbreaks to Near-Ceiling ASR Across Frontier Models in 2.46 Queries
entries.summary: BLUEPRINT, a multi-turn jailbreak evaluation framework combining Monte Carlo Tree Search over 18 social-influence factors with a cross-turn worldview simulation module, achieves near-ceiling attack success rates across six frontier open-weight and proprietary models while requiring the fewest average queries (2.46), and finds that making requests actionable and concrete is the single most potent resistance-bypassing factor.

entries.title: SEAL: Shared Expert Alignment Defends MoE Models Against Jailbreaks, Fine-Tuning Attacks, and Neuron Pruning (CCS 2026)
entries.summary: SEAL (accepted at ACM CCS 2026) identifies theoretically and empirically that always-activated shared experts in Mixture-of-Experts architectures can serve as a router-independent safety anchor, and shows a parameter-efficient plug-and-play adapter that reduces attack success rate by up to 60% across six attack scenarios combining harmful prompting, jailbreaks, malicious fine-tuning, and neuron pruning, at a capability cost of at most 1.4%.

entries.title: UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill Excludes AI Vendors, Placing Agentic AI Risk Entirely on Enterprise Deployers
entries.summary: The UK government rejected House of Lords amendments that would have placed AI vendors and frontier model developers within the scope of the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, opting instead for voluntary measures including the AI Security Institute and AI Cyber Security Code of Practice, which means regulated deploying organizations — not AI model vendors — bear the legal obligations.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: UK Cyber Bill Places Risk on Enterprise Deployers

entries.title: GERENCIA 360 MUSIC v. Suno and Bright Data: New Copyright Suit Over Scraping Licensed Streaming Services to Train AI Music Model
entries.summary: Music company GERENCIA 360 MUSIC filed suit on August 31, 2026 against Suno and Bright Data in the Northern District of California, alleging copyright infringement and DMCA violations arising from the scraping of copyrighted songs from licensed streaming services to train Suno's generative AI music platform.

entries.title: 215,000 Fake AI Buying Guides Systematically Poisoning RAG Procurement Pipelines
entries.summary: Trellner Research found three coordinated websites published over 215,000 machine-generated software recommendation pages designed to be retrieved by AI systems rather than read by humans, with testing across 380 software categories showing 59.8% of citations returned by Perplexity pointed to domains outside the top 100,000 most-visited websites — exposing a direct integrity risk in any enterprise workflow using AI-grounded search for vendor selection.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: 215,000 Fake AI Buying Guides Poisoning RAG Pipelines

entries.title: Mistral Switches to Default Opt-In for Training Data on Consumer and Standard API Tiers, Creating GDPR Exposure
entries.summary: Mistral AI updated its data policy so that user conversations and uploaded documents are used for model training by default on its Vibe consumer and standard API tiers, while enterprise customers on Vibe Enterprise are opted out by default — creating separate compliance exposure under GDPR that must be managed independently for each tier.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: Mistral Default Opt-In Training Data Policy

entries.title: AI Agents Reshape Human Group Consensus Formation: Three Regimes, Agent-Led Norms Become More Abstract and Less Information-Dense
entries.summary: A controlled experiment in mixed human-AI groups finds three distinct consensus regimes depending on AI agent proportion — low AI proportion enables human-led consensus, intermediate proportions disrupt convergence, and high proportions restore strong consensus but shift it toward agent-led conventions that are more abstract, less information-dense, and more geometrically segmented than human-led conventions — with implications for AI governance of collective deliberation.
